newsitem.title: UK: IGC maintains 1997 world wheat output estimate.
newsitem.headline: IGC maintains 1997 world wheat output estimate.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) on Thursday left its estimate unchanged for the 1997 world wheat crop at 578 million tonnes, after production estimated at 581 million tonnes in 1996.

But the IGC altered 1997 estimates for leading producers China, Kazakhstan and Argentina. It raised its estimate for Chinese wheat production from 110 to 112 million tonnes for 1997, up from 109 million the previous year.

CIS countries would turn out 68.3 million tonnes of wheat, 1.4 million lower than the last estimate issued on May 1 but up on 63.3 million produced in 1996. Lower expected output in Kazakhstan was the main reason for the reduced estimate. The IGC pegged Kazakh production 1.0 million tonnes lower at 10.0 million, still an improvement on the 8.0 million in 1996.
But it raised its forecast for Argentine 1997 wheat output by 500,000 tonnes to 13.5 million. Argentina produced 15.8 million tonnes in 1996.
Output was also expected to decline in the U.S., Canada and Australia, to be partially offset by a significant recovery in central and eastern Europe.
World consumption in 1997/98 was forecast at 582 million tonnes, 1.0 up on the previous estimate. The forecast for world wheat stocks was raised by 1.0 million to 96 million.

Consumption and stocks for 1996/97 were estimated at 577 and 100 million tonnes respectively. The IGC said the forecast decline in wheat stocks should be seen mostly in importing regions, since those in the five major exporting countries might increase by two million tonnes to 38 million.
